sentences.text:
This appeal is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of compensation passed by the Fast Track Court, Basavakalyan, Dist: Bidar (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC.No.673/2010 dated 22.09.2012.
2.
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for both parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. For the sake of convenience, parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Claims Tribunal.

4. The brief facts of the case are:
On 3.10.2009 the claimant was proceeding towards his village form Basavakalyan in a cab bearing No KA-32/3664 when the said vehicle came near pond bridge of village Ujalamb at about 6 PM the driver of the said maxi drove it in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger to human life lost control over the vehicle and dashed to the bridge due to the accident, the petitioner has sustained dislocation of his left shoulder and sustained incised wound, he had taken treatment at Govt. hospital Manthal thereafter he has taken treatment at Umerga hospital and Vishwekar hospital Umerga.
Prior to the accident the claimant was hale and healthy, aged about 50 years was doing agricultural work and he was earning
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has been permanently disabled and lost source of income.
Thereby causing dent to him financially, mentally and physically.
Hence, he preferred a claim petition seeking compensation.
5. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared and filed written statement denying the contents of claim made by the petitioner and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
6. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
7. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal after considering the notional monthly income of the claimant awarded compensation of Rs.55,000/-.
8. Being aggrieved by the quantum of the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the present appeal is filed.
9. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, the Tribunal ought to have awarded adequate compensation.
10. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer supported the judgment and award of the Tribunal and therefore contended that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal be not disturbed.

11. A perusal of the impugned judgment reveals that at para 27 the Tribunal has observed that petitioner claims that he has sustained disability to the extent of 39% and produced disability Krishnappa S/O Shantappa Chinchole vs Laxmiputra S/O Maturi Gowde And Anr on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111706313/
2 certificate - Ex.P-5 issued by Dr.Nitin Loharekar, who is examined as PW2.

sentences.text: Further it is observed that during the course of cross examination of PW2 he has stated that the ribs are reunited and dislocation of shoulder is united.
Under such circumstances, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
Though Tribunal has rejected the claim towards loss of future income due to disability in para 28, the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.12,000/- towards loss of future income due to disability.

The Tribunal has not assigned any reasons as to how the Tribunal has calculated an amount of Rs.12,000/- towards loss of future income due to disability though it has rejected the claim towards loss of future income due to disability as observed in para 27.
12.
Considering the age, occupation and nature of injuries and disability certificate issued by PW2 as per Ex.P-5, it is just and proper to assess the disability at 13% to the whole body.
13. As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority the notional income has to be taken at Rs.5,500/- per month for the accidents of the year 2010.
The age of the claimant was 50 years at the time of accident.
Hence, proper multiplier applicable to the age group of claimant is '13'.
Then it comes to Rs.5,500/- x 12 x 13 x 13% = Rs.1,11,540/-, which is rounded off to Rs.1,12,000/-.

14. Considering the nature of injuries, period of treatment, medical bills, I am of the considered opinion that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be re- determined and re-calculated as under:-

Awarded by Enhanced by

Heads  No the Tribunal this Court  01 Towards pain and Rs.15,000/- Rs.40,000/-
 suffering

02 Medical expenses Rs.22,000/- Rs.22,000/-
 03 Loss of future income Rs.12,000/- Rs.1,12,000/-
 due to disability  04 Special diet, Rs.6,000/- Rs.15,000/-
 nourishment and  attendant charges  05 Loss of amenities, ---- Rs.30,000/-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (a) The appeal is allowed in part.
(b) The judgment and award passed by the  Tribunal in MVC.No.673/2010 dated 22.09.2012 is modified.
The compensation of Rs.55,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.2,23,400/-.

(c) The insurer is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
(d) The insurer is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(e) All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal shall stand intact.
(f) The registry is directed to transmit the trial Court records to the concerned tribunal forthwith along with copy of this order.

Sd/-
